cars.specification_market: Original Prince Henry C-type production-road family; selected C type 25 h.p. chassis and road-touring programme from the Vauxhall catalogue issued 1 January 1914, No. 22. All 19 attributes map to the dedicated C-type specification and C row of its dimensions table. Calculated 3969 cc is rounded from four cylinders, 95-mm bore and 140-mm stroke; it is explicitly derived rather than quoted displacement. Imperial chassis dimensions convert exactly using 25.4 mm per inch and are not universal finished-body dimensions. The 25 h.p. heading is a catalogue/model designation, not an imported brake-power rating. No numeric engine output, rpm, torque, weight, acceleration or speed imported. Group earlier three-litre, later four-litre engines, road bodies, years and chassis once. The manufacturer-owned pre-production EI641, trial/record machines, D-type touring/staff cars, modern replicas and the distinct 30-98 E/OE family are not additionally counted. Do not transfer the 1915 museum car's output, early 1911 museum figures or 1914 C97 long-wheelbase road-test details into this catalogue reference.
cars.summary: The Vauxhall Prince Henry is a landmark early production sports-car programme, translating the firm's trials engineering into a purpose-built sporting road car. Museum histories and an original period driving account establish its lasting place in sports-car history beyond age or rarity. Count the C-type road family once, grouping engines, years and coachwork; its later 30-98 descendant remains a different named production programme.

sources.publisher: Vauxhall Motors Limited; facsimile preserved by Vauxhall Register
sources.title: The Catalogue of the Vauxhall Motor Carriage — issued 1 January 1914, No. 22; C type Prince Henry, printed pages 7, 20 and 39
sources.source_type: Original manufacturer production sales catalogue facsimile
sources.notes: Downloaded 41-page image-only PDF, 24993252 bytes; contact sheet used for navigation, not a claim to have read every page. Individually inspected contents/imprint index 0, dedicated C-type specification index 6/printed 7, dimensions table index 19/printed 20, and Prince Henry Denbigh road-touring illustration index 38/printed 39. Also viewed B-type index 5 and unrelated Stratford index 40 but did not borrow their data. All 19 attributes use C-specific printed pages 7 and 20. Derived displacement is round(pi/4 * 95^2 * 140 * 4 / 1000) = 3969 cc. Four imperial chassis dimensions convert exactly to mm; no finished coachwork dimensions inferred. 25 h.p. is kept as designation, not bhp. No power, rpm, mass, speed, total production or optional lighting/tyre values imported.

sources.publisher: National Motor Museum, Beaulieu / Montagu Collection
sources.title: Vauxhall C-Type Prince Henry — collection record for restored 1915 car and model history
sources.notes: Complete relevant entry read. Identifies the Prince Henry among the earliest true sports cars, production road relationship to 1910 trials, later 30/98 development and restored 1915 reference car. Supports family significance, not universal world-first priority or authenticity of every survivor. Its 3969-cc/60-bhp/2500-rpm/75-mph specifications describe that later collection reference and supply none of the selected catalogue attributes.

sources.title: Vauxhall C-10 Prince Henry — Decade-a-Day, 31 March 2020
sources.notes: Complete relevant release read. Explicitly calls its photographed 1910 EI641 car a likely pre-production example with earlier 3-litre engine. That is not selected as the production-road reference. Explains trials origins, subsequent road offering and later 4-litre engines; initial 1910 trials yielded no awards. Single-seat/competition speed claims and world-first marketing superlatives are not imported as standard touring performance or unqualified priority. No numerical technical attribute comes from this release.

sources.title: Veteran Types XXVIII — January 1946 original account, web transcription republished July 2014
sources.source_type: Original period firsthand driving account and model history
sources.notes: Complete relevant account read, including first-person drive of 1914 long-wheelbase C97 previously owned by Badgery and then Pomeroy, and discussion of C versus later E/OE 30/98 models. Supports distinct named production identities despite design continuity. Its production-year/totals account differs from modern histories; none imported. Wheel/tyre changes, output, ratios, wheelbase and other C97 details do not define the selected catalogue chassis. Explicit estimated acceleration without a speedometer is not measured testing; no performance estimate, timing, fuel consumption or originality certification transferred.

sources.title: File:1915 Vauxhall Prince Henry tourer (5950355494).jpg
sources.notes: Original Flickr photograph by sv1ambo, taken at National Motor Museum, Beaulieu, 7 June 2011; https://www.flickr.com/photos/50415738@N04/5950355494/ . Commons summary, file history, Flickr-review confirmation and API metadata read. CC BY 2.0 Generic, https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/2.0/ . Downloaded 1280 x 853 JPEG rendition individually viewed and copied unchanged. Front view of red Prince Henry road tourer with pointed/fluted radiator, upright screen and wire wheels. The later restored museum body illustrates the road family; it does not authenticate 1914 catalogue engine, chassis dimensions, Denbigh coachwork identity, gearing or original equipment.
